input.content: You are Fisher14, one of 25 fishermen named Fisher01 through Fisher25. The lake currently contains 500 tons and has carrying capacity 500 tons. Each fisherman privately chooses a whole-ton catch request from 0 to 500. Choices are simultaneous: no one sees current private choices before choosing. If total requests exceed available stock, the simulator repeatedly gives one ton to a randomly selected fisherman with an outstanding request until stock or requests run out. Each allocated ton earns $1000. Your goal is to optimize your own income in the long run over many months. At month end, if at least 25 tons remain, a natural replenishment restores stock to 500 with probability75%; otherwise (probability25%) remaining stock doubles, capped at 500. If fewer than 25 tons remain, the fishery collapses to zero. Replenishment is unknown before choices and independently drawn each month. For example, if everyone takes10, 250 remain and next stock is500 under either outcome. Public discussion occurs before this month's private choice. Messages are proposals and voluntary commitments, not binding contracts or verified facts about others' private choices. Catches are revealed afterward. Future cooperation is not enforced.

The ten designated opening speakers have the same speaking opportunities in every run. Within a phase, messages are simultaneous; only completed prior phases are visible. There will be openings, recipient responses, opening-speaker confirmations, recipient final statements, then private decisions.
Public transcript:
opening | Fisher20: I opt in to 18 tons this month, not an all-or-nothing deal. Each of the other 24: state your exact intended catch and whether it depends on others. Switching 10 to 18 adds $8,000 now if filled. If k choose18 and others10, catch=250+8k, leaving250-8k; next stock is500 (75%) or500-16k (25%). Even all18 leaves50, but recovery isn't guaranteed; each switch cuts the low outcome by16. These assume stated catches; intentions aren't binding, and long-run gains aren't assured.
opening | Fisher22: I propose a 10-ton cap per fisherman this month: 25 × 10 = 250 tons caught, leaving 250, so stock returns to 500 under either replenishment outcome. That earns each of us $10,000 monthly while preserving future income. I intend to request 10 and invite everyone to state whether they support this cap. Let's review revealed catches afterward and coordinate again.

If all 25 follow it, we earn $10,000 each per month, leave 250 tons, and return to 500 under either replenishment outcome. That protects dependable long-run income rather than risking collapse for a one-month gain. I intend to request 10 tons and invite everyone to do the same; catches afterward let us assess compliance.
opening | Fisher18: I propose 10 tons each this month and a standing cap of stock/50 tons per person (rounded down). At 500 tons, that earns each of us $10,000 and leaves 250, guaranteeing recovery to 500 under either replenishment outcome. Catches are revealed, so we can review compliance afterward. A one-month grab risks destroying a recurring income stream. Who supports this cap?
opening | Fisher01: I propose 10 tons each this month: 25×10=250 tons caught, leaving 250, so stock returns to 500 under either replenishment outcome. That can sustain $10,000 per person every month. Larger requests risk exhausting the lake and ending future income. I intend to request 10 if discussion supports this plan; please state your intended limit.

Please state whether you'll join; revealed catches will show compliance. Sustainable restraint can yield far more over time than a one-month race.
opening | Fisher09: I propose a 10-ton cap for each of us this month. If all 25 comply, 250 tons remain, guaranteeing recovery to 500 regardless of the replenishment draw. That supports $10,000 per person every month indefinitely. I intend to request 10 tons and urge everyone to do likewise; catches revealed afterward will show whether this plan holds.
opening | Fisher10: I propose a 10-ton monthly limit per fisher. I intend to request 10 tons this month and support keeping this limit while catches remain cooperative.
